title: start-record-detached.ps1 is not detached from its CALLER: Start-Process -RedirectStandardOutput/-RedirectStandardError forces UseShellExecute=false, so the child inherits the caller's stdio handles and any pipe-reading caller blocks for the recording's entire lifetime.
evidence: Measured 2026-09-27 with a minimal repro (8s child): WITH redirects 10.2s wall for the launching powershell pipeline, WITHOUT redirects 2.3s. Reproduced through the real launcher: printed 'started detached record: pid 41852' immediately but the bash pipeline did not return for 32.7s (the fixture's own lifetime). PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by the ISS-323 fix: the pnpm version carried the identical redirects.
fix_direction: Not blocking U5: task-scheduler.ts launches via a one-off Windows Scheduled Task, which reads no pipe (its only symptom there is a task row that shows 'running' for the webinar's duration). Affects programmatic/CLI callers that capture output. A fix must not trade away the ISS-323 liveness gate, which REQUIRES waiting on the child: a two-stage launch (outer Start-Process with no redirects, inner stage doing the redirected launch) detaches cleanly but cannot report the real pid or the liveness verdict back to the caller. Needs a design call before building.

title: the ISS-323 fix re-introduced silent argv corruption: per-argument quoting escaped only the quote character, so an argument ending in a backslash swallowed every argument after it
evidence: scripts/webinar/start-record-detached.ps1 (c8cbbf4) quoted each argument as WRAP + replace(quote -> backslash-quote). That is not CommandLineToArgvW escaping: a trailing backslash run is emitted undoubled, so the final backslash escapes the closing quote we added and the argument never closes. The reviewer reproduced it standalone on this machine with args [zoom-url, Ashoka \"Educator\" Dialogues, trailingback+backslash, --until, 12:30]: the child argv-dump received three arguments merged into one and --until / 12:30 vanished as distinct entries. Reachable, not contrived -- the title is partly email/candidate-sourced free text (see the ISS-317 note at packages/meeting-bot/src/calendar/task-scheduler.ts:16-30), so a pasted path fragment ending in a backslash is ordinary input. Also established by the same repro: Windows PowerShell 5.1 Start-Process -ArgumentList joins the array into ONE raw command line with NO escaping of its own, so exact quoting is entirely the caller s job. Same silent-corruption class as ISS-323(c) itself; contained only by the new liveness gate, which turns it into a loud failure rather than a silent one.
fix_direction: Implemented the real Win32 algorithm in Quote-Win32Argv (start-record-detached.ps1:95-118): walk each backslash run, double it when it precedes a quote or the end of the argument, single-escape the quote. Verified: a URL with & and an embedded quote already round-tripped and still do.
regression_check: scripts/webinar/start-record-detached.test.mjs -- "review finding: a title ending in a backslash (and one holding a quote) must not swallow the arguments after it": asserts the hostile title arrives as ONE argv entry AND that --until / 23:59 survive as their own entries. 4/4 pass. ADDITION to the ISS-323 corpus, never a substitution for the ledger cases (D-015). Checker cycle-1: independently reverted Quote-Win32Argv to the naive scheme in a throwaway copy -- this regression test alone went red (actual 'Ashoka "Educator" Dialogues C:\\share" ' vs expected trailing backslash preserved), the other 3 tests stayed green.

title: the absolute openCapMs branch shipped with no test, so the one mechanism that stops a chatty-but-never-opening bring-up existed only on inspection
evidence: All four ISS-324 tests in packages/meeting-bot/src/capture/obs-windows.test.ts set openCapMs: 20_000, far past any test runtime, so only the opened and stalled outcomes were ever executed -- the cap branch was dead code as far as the suite was concerned and could have been deleted silently. It is exactly the branch that prevents the evasion the reviewer probed for: a child emitting progress faster than openStallMs resets lastProgressAt forever, and only the cap can end that run.
fix_direction: Added a fifth test with openStallMs 400 / openCapMs 1_200 against the progress-then-open fixture at LKB_FIXTURE_TICKS 10000, tick 100ms: every tick resets the stall window, so the cap is the only possible terminator. Asserts the message attributes the cap, names the stuck stage, and that it ends well inside 10s -- a stall-only implementation would never end.
regression_check: obs-windows.test.ts "ISS-324 - a child that reports progress forever cannot outlive the absolute cap"; suite 8/8 on that file, 251/251 across meeting-bot, tsc clean. Checker cycle-1: independently neutered the openCapMs comparison in a throwaway copy (if (false && Date.now() - startedAt >= capMs)) -- this test alone went red, failing the /cap/ attribution assertion (actual message named 'child exited' with no cap reference).
